narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 94.7% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a very strong risk signal, so the admissions decision treated your application as too high-risk to admit.

The strongest reason was your third-year class standing: your third-year decile is 1, far from the accepted-student average of about 5.79. This was the top factor and pushed the prediction toward failure. Your first-year decile was the second most important factor; at 1 versus an accepted average of 6.00, it also pushed toward failure. The third-ranked factor was your undergraduate GPA. At 3.00 versus an accepted average of 3.23, it was the only one of the top three influences that pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the two standing factors. Family income and full-time status did not rank among the top drivers.

To move forward, ask admissions for feedback and whether you can submit an addendum explaining your academic trajectory. Focus on evidence of improved academic performance, especially in upper-level coursework, and seek pre-law or admissions advising. If possible, strengthen your academic record or retake the LSAT before reapplying, and consider schools or programs with strong bar-preparation support.
